transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what finally got me to come in here is that my work is really starting to suffer. I'm an electrician, and lately, I just... I can't seem to keep my focus on one thing. 

Like, if I'm sitting down to look at an estimate or fill out a code form, I get pulled off track so easily. It could be a tool making a noise in the background, my phone buzzing with a text, or even just some new idea I get about reorganizing the workshop. I'll drop what I'm doing and focus on that instead. Because of it, my jobs are starting to get all mixed up, and I can't really afford for that to happen. I just need to figure out how to keep my head straight so I can actually get my work done.
Did you have similar problems with focus or staying organized during childhood?

No, not really. I mean, growing up, I never had issues like this. I did alright in school... I could sit down and get my work done without getting distracted by every little thing. This whole problem where my brain just gets pulled in a hundred different directions, it's... it's pretty recent, honestly. It definitely wasn't a problem when I was a kid.
How would you describe the quality of your sleep lately?

My sleep has been pretty strange, honestly. For months now, I've only been getting maybe three or four hours a night. I'll just pop out of bed before dawn, and the weird thing is, I don't feel tired at all. I feel completely rested, like I had a full eight hours. I'll wake up feeling ready to go—pricing materials, answering emails, or sketching out a new electrical system. It's just... I'm up and running before the sun's even out.
During the period when you’ve been sleeping only three or four hours, have you felt unusually elevated or unusually irritable?

Yeah, honestly, it's a bit of both. I'll get in this really big, pumped-up mood... like, I'll be talking about how our little shop is about to become the main solar outfit in town, and I just feel great about it. But then, if my wife or one of the apprentices questions the plan at all, I can just flip. I get really sharp with them over nothing. So, yeah, I'm feeling really good and driven, but I guess I do get pretty irritable if someone pushes back on my ideas.
During this period of sleeping very little and feeling unusually driven, have you used any recreational drugs or other substances to get high or stay awake?

No, I haven't. I mean, I don't really do drugs or anything like that. And I definitely don't need anything to stay awake right now. Like I said, I just wake up and I'm already wired and ready to go. So, no, no substances or anything. Just coffee sometimes, but nothing else.
Have you ever been hospitalized because of this energized and irritable period?

No, I haven't. I mean, I know I get pretty intense and snap at people sometimes, but it's never gotten to the point where I had to go to a hospital or anything like that. I'm just out there working and doing my thing.

Yeah, I guess it is causing some real issues. Um, with work, clients have actually started complaining about missed details on jobs, or mixed-up scheduling. And the guys working under me... my apprentices, they just don't really trust my direction the way they used to. 

And at home... it's pretty rough right now. The mortgage and the business, it's just turning into constant arguments. My wife feels like I'm putting everything we've built at risk. So, yeah, it's definitely causing problems.
Before this current period, have you ever had another distinct period when you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt good and got a lot done, but nothing like this. This is... this is different. I've never felt this wired for this long before.
